recorded: BEFORE the test reference focal was opened
sigma_scene_note: equals the frozen floor for most videos: with all 381 frames AnyCalib's frame-to-frame log-MAD is below 0.02, so the scene term is very steep
reading: The hand score is NOT flat - it varies about 2x across the candidate window. What dominates is the scene term: with every frame of a 381-frame video the per-frame MAD sits at the frozen floor, making the scene penalty steep relative to the hand term's LOCAL slope near q=1. Under the pre-registered lambda grid (max 4) the hand term therefore rarely changes the chosen candidate.
decision: The lambda grid and the sigma definition are pre-registered (spec section 32, inherited from CAM-EXP-009.4) and are NOT widened now. Inflating lambda after seeing that the term is inert would be tuning the protocol to manufacture a non-null result. The measured movement rate is reported as part of the finding so the size of the gain is interpretable.
two_bugs_fixed_before_this: q_grid did not contain q=1.0 exactly, so lambda=0 did not reproduce scene-only (-0.65 % offset); now snapped to exactly 1.0
the hand score was normalised over the whole absolute grid (~12x range) instead of the candidate window, matching CAM-EXP-009.4
